llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (autonomous product browsing, checkout, and multi-chain crypto payments) matches the instructions and required surface — it is internally coherent, with only minor implementation/privacy notes to consider.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (agentic shopping, multi-chain checkout, order tracking) align with the SKILL.md and reference docs. The API endpoints, checkout workflow, and on-chain payment model are consistent with a marketplace that accepts crypto payments and applies token-holder discounts.

dimensions.detail: Instructions stay within shopping/checkout scope (search, product detail, create order, poll status). They explicitly instruct agents to request a user's wallet address for on-chain discount checks and to poll order status frequently while awaiting payment. This is expected for an autonomous checkout skill but raises privacy/usability considerations: the skill asks for wallet addresses (potentially sensitive) and instructs the agent to auto-follow recovery suggestions from error responses, which could cause aggressive retries or additional API calls if not rate-limited by the runtime.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate. One minor inconsistency: references/API.md documents GET /api/agent/me requiring an X-Moltbook-Identity header (agent runtime identity). The SKILL.md otherwise claims 'No API key or authentication needed.' Expect that calling /api/agent/me will use an agent-provided header if available; this may expose agent identity to the store if called.

llm.guidance: This skill is instruction-only and appears to do what it says: browse products, create orders, and coordinate cryptocurrency payments. Before installing or allowing autonomous use, consider the following: (1) The skill may ask customers for their wallet address to apply CULT discounts — treat wallet addresses as sensitive (they can be used for on-chain lookups) and confirm the user consents. (2) Crypto payments are irreversible — ensure the agent displays the exact on-chain payment address and amount and asks for an explicit user confirmation before directing funds. (3) The reference docs mention a Moltbook identity header (X-Moltbook-Identity) for one endpoint; verify whether your agent runtime will send that header and whether you are comfortable exposing that identity to forthecult.store. (4) Because the skill will poll order status (frequent requests), ensure your agent enforces rate limiting/backoff to avoid hitting rate limits. (5) Verify the HTTPS domain (https://forthecult.store) and consider testing with a low-value order first. Overall the skill is internally consistent, but review privacy and payment confirmation behavior before enabling autonomous checkout.
